### FINDING_2: **Important** (`risk-integration`) [scripts/redact-tmpdir-paths.sh:20-21](scripts/redact-tmpdir-paths.sh): The sed patterns rewrite **any** `/Users/<seg>/<seg>/` or `/home/<seg>/<seg>/` prefix to `<OPERATOR_REPO_PATH>/`, not only a real clone root. Concrete scenario: GitHub Actions logs often contain `/home/runner/work/...`; the first two segments are `runner` and `work`, so `/home/runner/work/` is rewritten to `<OPERATOR_REPO_PATH>/` even though that path is not an operator working tree. Published text becomes semantically wrong (mislabeled placeholder) and can confuse audits. Narrow the pattern (e.g. require a repo-shaped tail or an allowlist) or document that CI-style `/home/runner/work/` paths are intentionally mangled.

Published text becomes semantically wrong (mislabeled placeholder) and can confuse audits. Narrow the pattern (e.g. require a repo-shaped tail or an allowlist) or document that CI-style `/home/runner/work/` paths are intentionally mangled.

### FINDING_4: **Latent** (`risk-integration`) [skills/review/scripts/emit-tally.sh:63-95](skills/review/scripts/emit-tally.sh): The new strict path uses `grep -c '_OUTCOME=rejected$'` and `grep -n '_OUTCOME=rejected$'`. If `review-tally.env` ever carries Windows-style CRLF line endings, the `$` anchor fails, rejected lines disappear from the compact `rejected-findings.md`, and `review-summary.json` can undercount rejections while the ballot still shows rejections elsewhere.
